Rafael Morales: Quick brain dump — sketching an alternative to monolithic continuous-batching: separate the scheduler's "horizon" (how far ahead we look to form batches) from queue segmentation (how we partition requests). want quick opinions on tradeoffs before i draft an RFC.
Mei Chen: Curious — what's the main driver? tail latency, tenant fairness, or CPU/GPU utilization?
Rafael Morales: Short answer: all three, but the spike pattern we've seen is mostly due to mixed seq-lengths + aggressive prefetching. If horizon grows to cover long requests, short ones get stuck behind and latency spikes.
Ben K.: Idea: keep a small fast horizon (30–50ms) for short sequences and a longer background horizon for long sequences. admission picks queue based on estimated token length and tenant weight. avoids head-of-line blocking.
Alice Nguyen: That matches what we discussed earlier but with one twist: if we have segmented queues we need a cheap preemption token so a queued short request can cut the long request into two inflight batches or be fast-tracked. preemption is messy though.
Carla Perez: Preemption sounds risky for KV cache coherence on the GPU. breaking a long request mid- KV-warmup may lose efficiency. we should measure the cost of splitting vs letting the long run.
Mei Chen: Also need to think about admission fairness — if a tenant sends many short requests, they can monopolize the fast horizon. per-tenant credits needed.
Ben K.: Agreed. propose: 3 queue classes: fast (<=64 tokens), medium (65-512), long (>512). each class has its own horizon and an adjustable headroom token pool for emergency fast-track. tenant credits are debited at enqueue and reclaimed on completion.
Rafael Morales: sample config i sketched for experiments: ```
scheduler:
  queues:
    - name: fast
      max_horizon_ms: 40
      max_batch_tokens: 4096
    - name: medium
      max_horizon_ms: 120
      max_batch_tokens: 16384
    - name: long
      max_horizon_ms: 500
      max_batch_tokens: 65536
  headroom_pool_tokens: 10000
  tenant_credit_replenish_ms: 1000
```
Alice Nguyen: Looks reasonable. How do we pick queue on noisy length estimates? we only get token estimate from prompt size + cached model profile. need to avoid oscillation.
Ben K.: use conservative rounding: if estimate uncertain, favor next smaller bucket (prefer short). also allow runtime reclassification once tokenization completes but only before GPU KV is allocated.
Carla Perez: Observability: expose per-queue pending_ms distribution, headroom consumption, tenant credit balance, and KV-warmup count. That will help tune.
Mei Chen: i ran a tiny sim (3000 traces) with bucketed queues + headroom and saw 2.2x reduction in p99 for short requests, median improved 10–15%, but long-request throughput dropped ~6%. logs: ```
SIM: baseline p99(short)=420ms
SIM: bucketed p99(short)=190ms
SIM: throughput(long)=94% of baseline
```
Rafael Morales: good data. tradeoff seems acceptable. Need to document invariants: 1) no starvation — tenant credits prevent monopolization, 2) graceful degradation — headroom drains before preemptive eviction, 3) KV-affinity — avoid reclassification after KV pinned.
Alice Nguyen: Implementation complexity: we can keep a single admission API but return a queue label on enqueue. scheduler will keep per-queue ring buffers. preemption implemented as swap tokens + cancelable submission to GPU. may need driver-layer support for earlier cancellation.
Carla Perez: for cancelable submission we can fallback to letting the job finish but mark its cache as disposable and avoid reuse — cheaper than forcing driver cancel. downside: wasted KV work. quantify in next sim.
Ben K.: small optimization: allow batching across queue boundaries only when horizon alignment is within 5ms and all queues agree on model variant. reduces stragglers without cross-affinity mixing.
Rafael Morales: +1. Next steps i propose: (a) Ben to run larger sim with realistic tenant mixes and measure long throughput impact; (b) Mei to prototype observability metrics; (c) Alice/Carla to spike a safe preemption fallback (KV disposable) and estimate wasted work. I'll draft RFC next week incorporating these. @Ben K. @Mei Chen @Alice Nguyen please ack. :thumbsup:
Ben K.: ack. starting sims today.
Mei Chen: ack — will add dashboards and a few tracing hooks (trace id through admission -> batch -> gpu).
Alice Nguyen: ack. will spike preemption fallback PR and note driver limitations.
deploy-bot: scheduled test-job "scheduler-bucket-sim-01" submitted to staging cluster (job id: sj-8841). logs: https://staging.logs/sj-8841
Rafael Morales: thanks — will collect results and assemble RFC draft.
